note: Optional subjects: two papers of 250 marks each, so 500 of the 1,750 written marks. The pyq arrays are rebuilt by `python3 tools/pyq-papers.py optionals`; the copies arrays are curated by hand, because no publisher indexes its toppers' copies by optional subject and finding them means opening the section pages below.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.why: The most-taken optional after the humanities pair. Overlaps heavily with GS Paper I physical geography and with the environment and disaster-management sections of GS-III, which is most of its appeal. Paper I is systematic, Paper II is India.

topics.name: Geomorphology
points: Origin and evolution of the earth’s crusts
Physical conditions of the earth’s interior
Concepts of geomorphic cycles and Land scape development

topics.name: Climatology
points: Temperature and pressure belts of the world
Koppen’s Thornthwaite’s and Trewar Tha’s classification of world climate
Global climatic change, and role and response of man in climatic changes Applied climatology and Urban climate

topics.name: Oceanography
points: Bottom topography of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific Oceans
Temperature and salinity of the oceans
Heat and salt budgets, Ocean deposits
Law of the sea and marine pollution

topics.name: Biogeography
points: Factors influencing world distribution of plants and animals
Problems of deforestation and conservation measures

topics.name: Environmental Geography
points: Influence of man on ecology and environment
Global and regional ecological changes and imbalances

topics.name: Perspectives in Human Geography
points: Radical, behavioural, human and welfare approaches

topics.name: Economic Geography
points: World economic development: measurement and problems
World agriculture: typology of agricultural regions
World industries: location patterns and problems

topics.name: Population and Settlement Geography
points: Growth and distribution of world population
Population theories, world population problems and policies, Social well-being and quality of life
Types and patterns of rural settlements
Concept of primate city and rank-size rule

topics.name: Regional Planning
points: Types of regions and methods of regionalisation

topics.name: Models, Theories and Laws in Human Geography
points: Malthusian, Marxian and demographic transition models
Central Place theories of Christaller and Losch
Von Thunen’s model of agricultural location
Ostov’s model of stages of growth
Laws of international boundaries and frontiers

syllabus.title: Geography of India

topics.name: Physical Setting
points: Space relationship of India with neighbouring countries
Mechanism of Indian monsoons and rainfall patterns
Natural vegetation, Soil types and their distributions

topics.name: Resources
points: Land, surface and ground water, energy, minerals, biotic and marine resources, Forest and wild life resources and their conservation

topics.name: Agriculture
points: land holdings, land tenure and land reforms
Cropping pattern, agricultural productivity, agricultural intensity, crop combination, land capability
Green revolution and its socio-economic and ecological implications

topics.name: Industry
points: Locational factors of cotton, jute, textile, iron and steel, aluminium, fertiliser, paper, chemical and pharmaceutical, automobile, cottage and agro-based industries
Industrial houses and complexes including public sector undertakings

topics.name: Transport, Communication and Trade
points: Road, railway, waterway, airway and pipeline net works and their complementary roles in regional development
Growing importance of ports on national and foreign trade
Developments in communication and information technology and their impacts on economy and society

topics.name: Cultural Setting
points: Major tribes, tribal areas and their problems
Growth, distribution and density of population
Demographic attributes: sex-ratio, age structure, literacy rate, work-force, dependency ratio, longevity
migration (inter-regional, intraregional and international) and associated problems

topics.name: Settlements
points: Types, patterns and morphology of rural settlements

topics.name: Regional Development and Planning
points: Experience of regional planning in India
Planning for backward area, desert, drought-prone, hill tribal area development
Regional planning and development of island territories

topics.name: Political Aspects
points: International boundary of India and related issues
Geopolitics of South Asia and Indian Ocean realm

topics.name: Contemporary Issues
points: Ecological issues: Environmental hazards: landslides, earthquakes, Tsunamis, floods and droughts, epidemics
Changes in patterns of land use
Principles of environmental impact assessment and environmental management
Problems of agrarian and industrial unrest
Concept of sustainable growth and development

syllabus.note: Candidates will be required to answer one compulsory map question pertinent to subjects covered by this paper.

subjects.name: Law
subjects.why: Small candidate pool and a syllabus that rewards precision over volume. Overlaps with GS-II on the Constitution, and with GS-IV on jurisprudence. Paper I is constitutional and international law, Paper II is criminal, tort, contract and contemporary legal developments.

topics.name: Constitution and Constitutionalism:The distinctive features of the Constitution
Fundamental Rights—Public interest litigation; Legal Aid; Legal services authority
Relationship between Fundamental rights, Directive principles and Fundamental duties
Constitutional Position of the President and relation with the Council of Ministers
Supreme Court and the High Courts
Centre, States and local bodies
points: Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
Administrative relationship among Union, State and Local Bodies

topics.name: Services under the Union and the States
points: Recruitment and conditions of services; Constitutional safeguards; Administrative tribunals
Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions—Power and functions

topics.name: Principle of Natural Justice—Emerging trends and judicial approach
Separation of powers and constitutional governance
Nature and Definition of International Law
Relationship between International Law and Municipal Law
Law of the sea: Inland Waters,Territorial Sea, Contiguous Zone, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and High Seas
Individuals: Nationality, statelessness; Human Rights and procedures available for their enforcement
Territorial jurisdiction of States, Extradition and Asylum
Treaties : Formation, application, termination and reservation
United Nations : Its principal organs, powers and functions and reform
Lawful recourse to force : aggressions, self-defence, intervention
Fundamental principles of international humanitarian law—International conventions and contemporary developments
Legality of the use of nuclear weapons; ban on testing of nuclear weapons; Nuclear non- proliferation treaty, CTST
International Terrorism, State sponsored terrorism, Hijacking, International Criminal Court
New International Economic Order and Monetary Law : WTO, TRIPS, GATT, IMF, World Bank
Protection and Improvement of the Human Environment : International Efforts
General principles of Criminal liability : mens rea and actus reus, mens rea in statutory offences
Kinds of punishment and emerging trends as to abolition of capital punishment
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and subsequent legislative developments
Liability based upon fault and strict liability; Absolute liability

parts.title: Law of Contracts and Mercantile Law

topics.name: Void, voidable, illegal and unenforceable agreements
Contract of indemnity, guarantee and insurance
Sale of goods and hire purchase
Information Technology Law including Cyber Laws—Concept, purpose/prospects

subjects.name: Agriculture
subjects.why: The science optional with the widest overlap into General Studies: the agriculture, food security, irrigation and subsidy sections of GS-III are most of Paper I's ground, and cropping patterns and land reform reach into GS-I. Rewards candidates who already have the background, since both papers are technical rather than discursive. Paper I is ecology, soils, agronomy, water management and horticulture; Paper II is genetics and plant breeding, plant physiology, biotechnology, plant protection and animal science.

topics.name: Ecology and its relevance to man, natural resources, their sustainable management and conservation
points: Physical and social environment as factors of crop distribution and production
cropping pattern as indicators of environments
Environmental pollution and associated hazards to crops, animals and humans
Climate change—International conventions and global initiatives
Green house effect and global warming
Advance tools for ecosystem analysis—Remote Sensing (RS) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

topics.name: Cropping patterns in different agro-climatic zones of the country
points: Impact of high-yielding and short-duration varieties on shifts in cropping patterns
Concepts of various cropping, and farming systems
Package of practices for production of important cereals, pulses, oil seeds, fibres, sugar, commercial and fodder crops

topics.name: Important features, and scope of various types of forestry plantations such as social forestry, agro-forestry, and natural forests: Propagation of forest plants
points: Conservation of forest flora and fauna

topics.name: Weeds, their characteristics, dissemination and association with various crops; their multiplications; cultural, biological, and chemical control of weeds
Soil—physical, chemical and biological properties
points: Processes and factors of soil formation
Mineral and organic constituents of soils and their role in maintaining soil productivity
Essential plant nutrients and other beneficial elements in soils and plants
Principles of soil fertility, soil testing and fertiliser recommendations, integrated nutrient management Biofertilizers
Losses of nitrogen in soil, nitrogen-use efficiency in submerged rice soils, nitrogen fixation in soils
Soil factors affecting green house gas emission

topics.name: Soil conservation, integrated watershed management
points: Dry land agriculture and its problems
Technology for stabilising agriculture production in rain fed areas

topics.name: Water-use efficiency in relation to crop production, criteria for scheduling irrigations, ways and means of reducing run-off losses of irrigation water
points: Drainage of water-logged soils, quality of irrigation water, effect of industrial effluents on soil and water pollution

topics.name: Farm management, scope, importance and characteristics, farm planning
points: Economics of different types of farming systems
Marketing management strategies for development, market intelligence
role of co-operatives in agricultural economy
types and systems of farming and factors affecting them

topics.name: Agricultural extension, its importance and role, methods of evaluation of extension programmes, socio-economic survey and status of big, small and marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers; Training programmes for extension workers
points: Role of Krishi Vigyan Kendra’s (KVK) in dissemination of Agricultural technologies
Non-Government Organisation (NGO) and self-help group approach for rural development

topics.name: Cell structure, function and cell cycle
points: Synthesis, structure and function of genetic material
Chromosome structure, chromosomal aberrations, linkage and cross-over, and their significance in recombination breeding
Mutation—and their role in crop improvement
Heritability, sterility and incompatibility, classification and their application in crop improvement
Cytoplasmic inheritance, sex-linked, sex-influenced and sex-limited characters

topics.name: History of plant breeding
points: Modes of reproduction, selfing and crossing techniques
Origin, evolution and domestication of crop plants, center of origin, law of homologous series, crop genetic resources— conservation and utilization
Application of principles of plant breeding, improvement of crop plants
Molecular markers and their application in plant improvement
Pure-line selection, pedigree, mass and recurrent selections, combining ability, its significance in plant breeding
Breeding for disease and pest resistance
Role of interspecific and intergeneric hybridization
Role of genetic engineering and biotechnology in crop improvement Genetically modified crop plants

topics.name: Seed production and processing technologies
points: Seed certification, Seed testing and storage
DNA finger printing and seed registration
Role of public and private sectors in seed production, and marketing
Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) issues, WTO issues and its impact on Agriculture

topics.name: Principles of Plant Physiology with reference to plant nutrition, absorption, translocation and metabolism of nutrients
Enzymes and plant pigments; photosynthesis—modern concepts and factors affecting the process, aerobic and anaerobic respiration; C3, C4 and CAM mechanisms
points: Plant growth substances and their role in crop production
Physiology of seed development and germination
Stress physiology—draught, salt and water stress

topics.name: Major fruits, plantation crops, vegetables, spices and flower crops
points: package practices of major horticultural crops
Protected cultivation and high tech horticulture
Post-harvest technology and value addition of fruits and vegetables
Role of fruits and vegetables in human nutrition

topics.name: Diagnosis of pests and diseases of field crops, vegetables, orchard and plantation crops and their economic importance
points: Classification of pests and diseases and their management
Biological control of pests and diseases
Epidemiology and forecasting of major crop pests and diseases
Pesticides, their formulation and modes of action

topics.name: Food production and consumption trends in India
points: Availability of foodgrains, per capita expenditure on food
Trends in poverty, Public Distribution System and Below Poverty Line population, Targeted Public Distribution System (PDS), policy implementation in context to globalization
Relation of food production to National Dietary Guidelines and food consumption pattern
Food based dietary approaches to eliminate hunger

Nutrient deficiency—Micro nutrient deficiency: Protein Energy Malnutrition or Protein Calorie Malnutrition (PEM or PCM), Micro nutrient deficiency and HRD in context of work capacity of women and children
Food grain productivity and food security
